* U.S. [[United States Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Colin Powell]] says that thirty nations have joined with the United States in a "coalition of the willing" to remove [[Saddam Hussein]] from power, with another 15 quietly promising their support.  See [[Worldwide government positions on war on Iraq]].
* [[Naji Sabri]], the [[Iraq]]i foreign minister, calls U.S. President [[George W. Bush]] "a [[War crime|war criminal]]", "tyrant", "despot" and "[[Idiot (usage)|idiot]]". He also claims that evacuation of [[UNIKOM]] from the [[demilitarized zone]] violates the [[UN]] resolution of 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cbc.ca/stories/2003/03/18/iraqreaxn030318 |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050318175925/http://www.cbc.ca/stories/2003/03/18/iraqreaxn030318 |archive-date=2005-03-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Approximately US$1 billion is stolen from the [[Central Bank of Iraq]], anticipating the imminent [[Iraq War|bombing]] of [[Baghdad]].
* The [[United Kingdom Parliament]] votes in to grant [[18 March 2003 Parliamentary Approval for the invasion of Iraq|Parliamentary Approval for the invasion of Iraq]].
